column3: “Good” is rendered “most beautiful,” and NASB adds “also.”
“Every desirable thing of your eyes” is rendered “whatever is desirable in your eyes.”
“Know and see” is rendered “observe and see,” and “seeking trouble” as “looking for trouble.”
“At my feet” is rendered “who follow me.”
NASB supplies “Tell him” and “his armor … it off.”
NASB names “Ben-hadad,” and “booths” as “temporary shelters”; “Set yourselves” is rendered “Station yourselves.”
“Struck down each his man” is rendered “killed each his man.”
“Struck down among Aram” is rendered “killed the Arameans.”
“At the return of the year” is rendered “at the turn of the year.”
The Hebrew has the plural form for “God” with singular sense; NASB has “Their gods are gods of the mountains.”
“Which fell from you” is rendered “that you have lost,” and “horse like the horse” as “horse for horse.”
Close to the Hebrew; NASB adds “therefore.”
“A room in a room” is rendered “an inner chamber.”
